# 1. Setup & Environment

We load required packages using `pacman::p_load()`, ensuring all necessary libraries for data wrangling, missing data profiling, and visualization are installed and attached.

```{r libraries}
if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse,  # covers dplyr, ggplot2, lubridate, tidyr, stringr, purrr, forcats
  janitor,    # data hygiene (clean_names, tabyl)
  skimr,      # broad EDA summary
  naniar,     # missingness patterns
  glue        # string interpolation
)
```

# 3. Reusable Utility Functions

To maintain consistent data exploration, testing, and validation across all files, we establish reusable helper functions.



```{r utility_functions}
# --- Helper: Centered Section Header ---
print_header <- function(heading, total_width = 70) {
  pad_len <- max(1, floor((total_width - (nchar(heading) + 2)) / 2))
  cat("\n\n", strrep("=", pad_len), " ", heading, " ", strrep("=", pad_len), "\n\n", sep = "")
}

# --- Comprehensive Data Overview ---
show_data_overview <- function(df, name, mcar_t=TRUE) {
  print_header(glue("{name}: Structure & Skim"))
  glimpse(df)
  print(skim(df))

  print_header(glue("{name}: Missingness Summary"))
  # naniar::miss_var_summary computes n_missing and pct_missing automatically
  miss_summary <- naniar::miss_var_summary(df) |>
    filter(n_miss > 0)
  print(as.data.frame(miss_summary), row.names = FALSE)

  print_header(glue("{name}: MCAR Test"))
  
  if(mcar_t){
    print(naniar::mcar_test(df))
  }
}

# --- Categorical Variable Profiling ---
profile_categorical_variables <- function(df, factor_cols, name) {
  print_header(glue("{name}: Profiling Categorical Variables"))
  
  # tabyl handles multiple columns cleanly when piped through purrr::map
  factor_cols |>
    set_names() |>
    map(\(col) df |>
    tabyl({{ col }}) |>
    adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 2))
}

# --- Duplicate & Key Integrity Checks ---
check_for_duplicates <- function(df, id_col, name) {
  id_name <- rlang::as_name(ensym(id_col))
  
  print_header(glue("{name}: Duplicate Summary for `{id_name}`"))
  dupe_rows <- df |> get_dupes({{ id_col }})
  n_dupes <- nrow(dupe_rows)
  cat(glue("Found {n_dupes} duplicate record(s) involving key: `{id_name}`.\n\n"))

  print_header(glue("{name}: Rows with Conflicting Attributes"))
  conflicts <- df |>
    filter(n_distinct(pick(everything())) > 1, .by = {{ id_col }}) |>
    arrange({{ id_col }})
  print(conflicts)
  
  invisible(list(dupes = dupe_rows, conflicts = conflicts))
}

# --- Outlier Analysis (Tukey IQR + Faceted Visualizations) ---
check_for_outliers <- function(df, cols, name) {
  print_header(glue("{name}: Outlier Analysis (IQR Method)"))

  # Compute IQR stats vectorized across columns without row-wise loops
  summary_tbl <- df |>
    summarise(across(all_of(cols), list(
      q1    = \(x) quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q3    = \(x) quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      n     = \(x) sum(!is.na(x)),
      out   = \(x) {
        q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
        sum(x < (q[1] - 1.5 * diff(q)) | x > (q[2] + 1.5 * diff(q)), na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    ))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("Variable", ".value"), names_sep = "_") |>
    mutate(
      IQR = q3 - q1,
      Lower_Cutoff = round(q1 - 1.5 * IQR, 2),
      Upper_Cutoff = round(q3 + 1.5 * IQR, 2),
      Pct_Outliers = scales::percent(out / n, accuracy = 0.01)
    ) |>
    select(Variable, Q1 = q1, Q3 = q3, IQR, Lower_Cutoff, Upper_Cutoff, N_Outliers = out, Total = n, Pct_Outliers)

  print(as.data.frame(summary_tbl), row.names = FALSE)

  # Reshape for unified visualization
  df_long <- df |>
    select(all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
    drop_na(value)

  p_box <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = "", y = value)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", color = "midnightblue", outlier.colour = "firebrick") +
    facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
    labs(title = glue("{name}: Boxplots"), x = NULL, y = "Value") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

  p_hist <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = value)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
    facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
    labs(title = glue("{name}: Histograms"), x = "Value", y = "Count") +
    theme_minimal()

  print(p_box)
  print(p_hist)
}

# --- Claim Frequency Distribution ---
analyze_claims_distribution <- function(claims_df, name = "Claims") {
  print_header(glue("{name}: Claim Frequency per Policy"))
  
  dist_tbl <- claims_df |>
    count(policy.ID, name = "n_claims") |>
    tabyl(n_claims) |>
    adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 2)

  print(dist_tbl)
  invisible(dist_tbl)
}

# --- Structured Reporting ---
make_observations <- function(dataset_name, ...) {
  print_header(glue("Observations: {dataset_name}"))
  obs <- list(...)
  env <- parent.frame()
  
  walk2(seq_along(obs), obs, \(i, item) {
    cat(glue("{i}. {glue(item, .envir = env)}\n"))
  })
}
```

# 4. Pets Dataset: EDA & Cleaning

## 4.1 Exploratory Data Analysis

We profile the raw pet records, check for duplicate `pet.ID` entries, and validate breed names against the provided appendices.

```{r pets_eda}
show_data_overview(raw_pet_data, "Pets")

profile_categorical_variables(
  raw_pet_data,
  c(
    "pet.Type",
    "pet.Group",
    "pet.Gender",
    "pet.Offspring",
    "pet.Microchip",
    "pet.Origin"
  ),
  "Pets"
)

check_for_duplicates(raw_pet_data, pet.ID, "Pets")

check_for_outliers(
  raw_pet_data,
  c("pet.Age", "pet.Height", "pet.Weight"),
  "Pets"
)

# Validate breed names against appendix
check_breeds <- function(breed = "Dog",
                         appendix = appendix_breed_dogs,
                         df = raw_pet_data) {
  breeds_expected <- appendix |>
    str_replace_all("[\r\n.]+", " ") |>
    str_remove("\\.+$") |>
    str_squish() |>
    str_split_1("\\s*,\\s*")
  
  print_header(glue("Check discrepancies in `{breed}` breed"))
  breeds_actual <- as.list(
    df |>
      filter(pet.Type == breed & !is.na(pet.Breed)) |>
      select(pet.Breed) |>
      unnest(pet.Breed) |>
      unique() |>
      pull()
  )
  
  print(glue("{breed} breeds present in the data, but missing from appendix list:"))
  extra_breeds <- setdiff(breeds_actual, breeds_expected)
  cat(paste0(seq_along(extra_breeds), ". ", extra_breeds, "\n"), sep = "")
  
  return(extra_breeds)
}

extra_dog_breeds <- check_breeds("Dog", appendix_breed_dogs)
extra_cat_breeds <- check_breeds("Cat", appendix_breed_cats)

make_observations(
  "Pets",
  "pet.Age (1-18), pet.Height (4.9-32.9), and pet.Weight (3.1-137.9) fall into expected biological ranges.",
  "`p` in the MCAR test is significantly larger than 5%, confirming missing values are missing completely at random.",
  "Gender is coded with both `M` and `Male`, `F` and `Female`, requiring normalization to factors.",
  "Microchip is coded with both `No`, `Nope`, `Y`, `Yes`, requiring standardization.",
  "In pet.Group: `Non-Sporting` has two spellings ('Non-Sporting' and 'Non-sporting'), requiring consolidation.",
  "The {toString(extra_dog_breeds)} are dog breeds present in the data but missing from the appendix list; retained as valid population.",
  "There are 369 rows with duplicate pet.ID in Pets, out of which 32 have conflicting values mostly due to NA entries.",
  "In outlier analysis (1.5 * IQR), `pet.Age` and `pet.Height` exhibit 0 outliers, whereas `pet.Weight` exhibits 1,808 outliers (4.85% of total records) with values exceeding the upper cutoff of 106.6 lbs, driven by large/giant dog breeds.",
  "Weight seems to be heavily right skewed, with 4% outliers. Thus, a log transformation might be appropriate."
)
```

## 4.2 Cleaning & Deduplication

We recode factors and resolve duplicate records by choosing non-NA values.

```{r pets_cleaning}

# Recoding and consolidation
pets <- raw_pet_data |>
  mutate(
    pet.Type = as.factor(pet.Type),
    pet.Group = as.factor(
      case_match(pet.Group, "Non-sporting" ~ "Non-Sporting", .default = pet.Group)
    ),
    pet.Breed = as.factor(pet.Breed),
    pet.Gender = as.factor(
      case_match(pet.Gender, "F" ~ "Female", "M" ~ "Male", .default = pet.Gender)
    ),
    pet.Offspring = as.factor(pet.Offspring),
    pet.Microchip = as.factor(
      case_match(pet.Microchip, "Nope" ~ "No", "Y" ~ "Yes", .default = pet.Microchip)
    ),
    pet.Origin = as.factor(pet.Origin)
  )



# Verify extra dog breeds distribution
pets |>
  filter(pet.Breed %in% extra_dog_breeds) |>
  count(pet.Breed, sort = TRUE)
# Seem to be well representative of the population. The data vendor probably
# shared an outdated appendix, which didn't have these four breeds.

# Deduplicate Pets: remove exact duplicates and resolve conflicting records by taking non-null values
cat(glue("Pet records before dedup: {nrow(pets)}\n\n"))

pets <- pets |>
  distinct() |>
  group_by(pet.ID) |>
  summarize(across(everything(), \(x) {
    v <- na.omit(x)
    if (length(v) > 0) v[1] else x[1]
  }), .groups = "drop")

cat(glue("Pet records after dedup: {nrow(pets)} (unique pets: {n_distinct(pets$pet.ID)})\n\n"))
```

# 5. Owners Dataset: EDA & Cleaning

## 5.1 Exploratory Data Analysis

We inspect demographics, check duplicate owner records, and validate `owner.PetCount` against the actual count of pet records.

```{r owners_eda}
show_data_overview(raw_owner_data, "Owners")

profile_categorical_variables(
  raw_owner_data,
  c("owner.Gender", "owner.Location", "owner.Channel", "owner.PetCount"),
  "Owners"
)

check_for_duplicates(raw_owner_data, owner.ID, "Owners")

check_for_outliers(
  raw_owner_data,
  c("owner.Age", "owner.CreditScore", "owner.PetCount"),
  "Owners"
)

make_observations(
  "Owners",
  "owner.Age (22-78), owner.CreditScore (300-850), and owner.PetCount (1-4) fall into valid ranges.",
  "`p` in the MCAR test is well above 5%, confirming missing values are Missing Completely at Random.",
  "Categorical variables (Gender, Location, Channel) are clean with no miscoding or invalid levels.",
  "There are 219 duplicate owner.ID records in the raw data, with 4 unique owners exhibiting conflicting records.",
  "The number of pets reported by the owner owner.PetCount is greater than or equal to the number of pets for that owner in the pets  dataset. This may be due to the fact that few owners (9.08%) have uninsured pets.",
  "Pet count of 5 and above are clearly outliers. It might be useful to make the pet count variable a factor and group"
)
```

## 5.2 Cleaning & Deduplication

We deduplicate owners by selecting the maximum recorded `owner.PetCount` and taking non-NA entries for all other attributes.

```{r owners_cleaning}
owners <- raw_owner_data |>
  group_by(owner.ID) |>
  summarize(
    owner.PetCount = max(owner.PetCount, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(-owner.PetCount, ~ na.omit(.x)[1]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    owner.Gender = as.factor(owner.Gender),
    owner.Location = as.factor(owner.Location),
    owner.Channel = as.factor(owner.Channel)
  )

stopifnot(n_distinct(owners$owner.ID) == nrow(owners))
```

# 6. Policy Dataset: EDA & Cleaning

## 6.1 Exploratory Data Analysis

We inspect policy periods, exposure distributions, and duplicate records.

```{r policy_eda}
show_data_overview(raw_policy_data, "Policy")

profile_categorical_variables(
  raw_policy_data,
  c("policy.NBRB"),
  "Policy"
)

check_for_duplicates(raw_policy_data, policy.ID, "Policy")

check_for_outliers(
  raw_policy_data,
  c("policy.Exposure"),
  "Policy"
)

make_observations(
  "Policy",
  "policy.Start and policy.End are character strings and require formatting to Date objects.",
  "Exposure is in (0, 1] range; records with zero exposure do not contribute to risk and must be excluded.",
  "`p` in the MCAR test is significantly above 5%, confirming missing values are Missing Completely at Random.",
  "policy.NBRB has miscoded categories ('NewBus' -> 'NB', 'RenBus' -> 'RB') requiring standardization.",
  "There are 0 duplicate policy.ID records found in the policy dataset."
)
```

## 6.2 Cleaning & Transformation

We filter out zero-exposure policies, convert date columns to `Date` types, and standardize `policy.NBRB`.

```{r policy_cleaning}
policy <- raw_policy_data |>
  filter(policy.Exposure > 0) |>
  mutate(
    policy.Start = date_decimal(policy.Start),
    policy.End = date_decimal(policy.End),
    policy.NBRB = as.factor(case_match(
      policy.NBRB,
      "NewBus" ~ "NB",
      "RenBus" ~ "RB",
      .default = policy.NBRB
    ))
  )

cat(glue("Policy records after filtering zero exposure: {nrow(policy)} (unique policies: {n_distinct(policy$policy.ID)})\n\n"))
```

## 7.1 Exploratory Data Analysis

We examine claim costs and the frequency of claims per policy.

```{r claims_eda}
show_data_overview(raw_claims_data, "Claims")

profile_categorical_variables(
  raw_claims_data,
  c("claim.Coverage"),
  "Claims"

check_for_duplicates(raw_claims_data, claim.ID, "Claims")

check_for_outliers(
  raw_claims_data,
  c("claim.Cost"),
  "Claims"
)

analyze_claims_distribution(raw_claims_data, "Claims")

make_observations(
  "Claims",
  "Zero missing values exist across all columns in the claims dataset.",
  "claim.Coverage contains two clean, consistent categories: 'Illness' and 'Accident'.",
  "84.8% of policies with claims have 1 claim, 12.8% have 2 claims, and remaining few have 3-5 claims.",
  "claim.Cost exhibits a right-skewed distribution with severe high-cost outliers typical of insurance loss data.",
  "There are zero duplicate claim.ID records."
)
```

## 7.2 Cleaning Claims

```{r claims_cleaning}
claims <- raw_claims_data |>
  mutate(
    claim.Coverage = as.factor(claim.Coverage)
  )
```

# 8. Dataset Merging & Final Validation

We merge the four datasets into a unified modeling dataset.

1. **Aggregate claims by `policy.ID`**: calculate claim count and separate losses for `Illness`, `Accident`, and `TotalLoss`.
2. **Left join `policy` to `pets` on `pet.ID`**.
3. **Left join to `owners` on `owner.ID`**.
4. **Left join to aggregated claims on `policy.ID`**, imputing non-claiming policies with 0 claims and \$0 loss.

```{r dataset_merge}
print_header("Merging Datasets: Policy + Pets + Owners + Claims")

# 1. Aggregate claims by policy
claims_agg <- claims |>
  group_by(policy.ID) |>
  summarize(
    n_claims = n(),
    illness_loss = sum(claim.Cost[claim.Coverage == "Illness"]),
    accident_loss = sum(claim.Cost[claim.Coverage == "Accident"]),
    total_losses = sum(claim.Cost),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
nrow(claims_agg)
n_distinct(claims_agg$policy.ID)
cat(glue("Aggregated claims: {nrow(claims_agg)} unique policies with claims.\n\n"))
```
Thus aggregated claims table has one row per policy.

```{r}

# 2. Join Policy to Pets on pet.ID
merged_df <- policy |>
  left_join(pets, by = "pet.ID")

nrow(anti_join(policy, pets, by = "pet.ID"))
```
No missing values were introduced due to the policy + pets join.

```{r}

# 3. Join with Owners on owner.ID
merged_df <- merged_df |>
  left_join(owners, by = "owner.ID")

nrow(anti_join(merged_df, owners, by = "owner.ID"))
```
No missing values were introduced due to the (policy, pets) + owners join.

```{r}

# 4. Join with Claims Aggregation on policy.ID
merged_df <- merged_df |>
  left_join(claims_agg, by = "policy.ID") |>
  mutate(
    n_claims = replace_na(n_claims, 0),
    illness_loss = replace_na(illness_loss, 0),
    accident_loss = replace_na(accident_loss, 0),
    total_losses = replace_na(total_losses, 0)
  )

nrow(merged_df)
nrow(anti_join(merged_df, claims_agg, by = "policy.ID"))
```
Not all policies generate claims, and in our case we have 62576 (85.88%) policies
that didn't generate a claim. We will replace NA values in claims_agg with 0.

```{r}
merged_df <- merged_df |> 
  # replace n_claims, illness_loss, accident_loss,
  # total_losses  NA values with 0
  mutate(across(starts_with("claims_agg"), \(x) replace_na(x, 0)))
```

Confirm the proportion of policies with zero claims

```{r}
merged_df |>
  summarize(
    n_zero_claims = sum(n_claims = sum(n_claims == 0)),
    pct_zero_claims = paste(round(mean(n_claims == 0)*100, 2),"%")
  )
```

About 86% of our dataset has no claims.

```{r}
df <- merged_df |>
  mutate(pure_premium = total_losses / policy.Exposure)

```


## 8.3 Post-Merge Profiling & Final Observations

Review pure premium distribution
```{r}
summary(df$pure_premium)
```
Confirm the proportion of policies with zero pure premium
```{r}
df |> 
  summarize(
    n_zero_pp = sum(pure_premium == 0),
    pct_zero_pp = round(mean(pure_premium == 0)* 100, 2)
  )
```

```{r post_merge_profiling}
show_data_overview(df, "Merged Dataset", mcar_t = FALSE)

make_observations(
  "Merged Dataset",
  "Policy dataset (exposure > 0) serves as the base population with {nrow(policy)} records.",
  "100% of policies successfully matched to a pet in `pets` (0 unmatched pet.IDs).",
  "100% of pet records successfully matched to an owner in `owners` (0 unmatched owner.IDs).",
  "Claims aggregated at policy level merged cleanly; non-claiming policies imputed with 0 claims and 0 losses.",
  "Final modeling dataset contains {nrow(merged_df)} records across {ncol(merged_df)} features ready for pure premium modeling."
)
```



```{r}

write.csv(df, "data/merged.csv", row.names=FALSE)

cat(glue("\nMerge completed successfully!\n"))
cat(glue("Final merged dimensions: {nrow(merged_df)} rows x {ncol(merged_df)} columns.\n\n"))
```
